note.text:
Physicists observe nature and try to understand it. They work in steps (the scientific method):
1. Observe something carefully.
2. Ask a question about it.
3. Suggest an answer that can be tested (a hypothesis).
4. Test it with an experiment.
5. Record and study the results.
6. Draw a conclusion, and share it.
A fair test changes only one thing at a time and keeps everything else the same. Scientists measure carefully, repeat experiments, and are honest about their results, even when the results show their idea was wrong.

worked_example.problem: Tabe wants to know if salt makes water boil faster. How can he make his test fair?
steps: Use two pots that are the same, with the same amount of water, on the same fire.
Add salt to one pot only: change just one thing.
Measure the time each pot takes to boil.
Repeat the test to check the result.
worked_example.answer: Change only the salt; keep everything else the same, measure, and repeat.

cards.idea: Scientists work in steps: observe, ask a question, suggest an answer, test it, record the results, conclude.
example: Observe: the black pot heats faster. Question: does colour matter? Test: two pots in the sun.

cards.idea: Each part of an investigation is one of these steps.
example: “Every ten minutes Bih writes the temperature in a table” is recording the results.

cards.idea: A fair test changes only one thing at a time and keeps everything else the same.
example: To test salt, both pots get the same water and the same fire; only one gets salt.

check.prompt: In a fair test, how many things do you change at a time?

wrong.explain: If two things change, you cannot tell which one caused the result.
Then you cannot tell what caused the result.
If nothing changes, there is nothing to test.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of the scientific method in order.

items.text: Suggest an answer to test (a hypothesis)

pick.t: Bih notices that water in a black pot gets hot faster than in a white pot.
pick.why: This is the step “Observe something carefully”.

pick.t: Bih asks: “Does the colour of a pot change how fast water heats up?”
pick.why: This is the step “Ask a question about it”.

pick.t: Bih thinks: “Black pots take in more heat from the sun.”
pick.a: Suggest an answer to test (a hypothesis)
pick.why: This is the step “Suggest an answer to test (a hypothesis)”.

pick.t: Bih puts the same amount of water in a black pot and a white pot, side by side in the sun.
pick.why: This is the step “Test it with an experiment”.

pick.t: Every ten minutes Bih reads the thermometer in each pot and writes the temperature in a table.
pick.why: This is the step “Record and study the results”.

pick.t: Bih says: “The black pot heated faster, so colour does matter.”
pick.why: This is the step “Draw a conclusion”.

distractors.text: Suggest an answer to test (a hypothesis)

misconceptions.explain: Not quite. Is Bih looking, asking, guessing, testing, writing results, or deciding?

questions.prompt: Ndi wants to test whether plants grow taller with fertiliser. Which plan is a fair test?

right.text: Two plants of the same kind, the same pot, soil, water and sunlight; fertiliser for one plant only.

wrong.text: One plant in the sun with fertiliser, one in the shade without.
wrong.explain: Two things change (sun and fertiliser), so we cannot tell which one made the difference.

wrong.text: Give both plants fertiliser and see which grows taller.
wrong.explain: Nothing is compared: both get fertiliser.
A scientist tests the idea with an experiment, not by asking opinions.

questions.prompt: One sentence about how scientists work is wrong. Which one?

right.text: Scientists repeat experiments to check their results.
A hypothesis is an answer that can be tested.
In a fair test only one thing is changed.

wrong.text: If the results do not match the idea, a scientist should change the results.
wrong.explain: Scientists must be honest: if the results disagree, they change the idea, not the results.

wrong.text: A scientist draws a conclusion before doing the experiment.
wrong.explain: The conclusion comes after testing and studying the results.
